title: Match the brackets
scenario: These brackets open and close. Is every opener matched by the right closer, in order?

intro.job: These brackets open and close. Is every opener matched by the right closer, in order?

idea.rule: A closer has to match the opener on top — same kind, not just any opener.
idea.detail: A stack is a pile of plates: you only touch the top one. Push every opener on the pile. When a closer comes, the opener on top is the most recent one still open — and it must be the SAME kind. A ')' on top of '[' means the brackets cross. At the end, the pile must be empty.

model_restatement: Check that every opening bracket is closed by the same kind of bracket, in the right order.

clarify.question: Isn't it enough to count openers and closers?
clarify.answer: No — they have to close in the right order, with the right kind.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Push each opener on a stack. When a closer comes, take the top opener off. At the end, if the stack is empty, it all matched. Print that.

checkpoints.prompt: After the second opener, what is stack?
Iteration 3: c is ')'. After line 6, what is stack?
With the fix — iteration 3: after line 8, what is ok?

why_line: stack.pop() takes whatever is on top without looking — the ')' pops a '[' and the ']' pops a '(', so the pile empties and crossed brackets look matched.

explain.rule: Popping without looking is a coat-check clerk who hands back whichever coat is on top — the ')' walks off with the '['.
explain.bridge: When ')' arrives, what must be on top of the pile for it to be a match?

fix.rule: Pop, then compare: the opener that comes off must be pairs[c] — the same kind as the closer.

walk.gloss: Opener? Put it on the pile.
Closer? The pile must not be empty, and the opener on top must be its pair.

contrast.right_note: it must be the matching kind

alternatives.code:
t = s
while True:
    shorter = t.replace('()', '').replace('[]', '').replace('{}', '')
    if shorter == t:
        break
    t = shorter
print(t == '')
alternatives.note: Peel off matching neighbours until none are left — correct, but it re-scans the whole string again and again.

hints: Iteration 3: which opener does ')' take off the pile?
pop() doesn't check the kind. ')' needs '('.
Compare what you pop with pairs[c]; if it isn't the match, it's not valid.

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — '}' finds '[' on top, and that's not its pair.

one_liner: A closer has to match the opener on top — same kind, not just any opener.
